idiom_name: base table plus subclass tables with key = foreign key, discriminator, mapper per class
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give the root class's table the primary key (and normally a type/discriminator code); give every subclass table a primary key that is also a foreign key to its superclass's table, and put only that class's declared attributes in it. Provide one mapper per class that owns the join path for that class, resolve the concrete class from the type code on polymorphic reads, and write every table of a path inside one transaction. Where an ORM offers a joined strategy, declare the mapping as metadata instead of hand-writing the join; where none exists, hand-write the join but keep it in one loader per class.
code_sketch:
party(id PK, name, kind)               -- base table: shared columns + discriminator
person(id PK FK -> party.id, birth_date)
organisation(id PK FK -> party.id, tax_no)
-- leaf-class query (one join):
  SELECT p.*, e.* FROM party p JOIN person e ON e.id = p.id WHERE p.id = ?
-- polymorphic query (discriminator routing):
  SELECT * FROM party; join the table named by kind
pitfalls: Subclass tables that do not repeat the superclass key as their own primary key lose the one-to-one guarantee and allow orphaned rows.
Omitting the type discriminator makes polymorphic reads instantiate base-class rows only.
Writing the base row and the subclass row in separate transactions leaves the schema inconsistent when the second statement fails.
Hand-written SQL that reads only the base table and assumes subclass columns are present.
